newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian interbank rates hold as demand rises.
newsitem.headline: Croatian interbank rates hold as demand rises.

text.p: Croatian interbank rates held firm on Monday in active trade as demand for kuna rose ahead of the fortnightly reserve payment, money market dealers said.
Fresh loans totalled a high 72.7 million kuna by 0930 GMT and still left an extra 60 million as most creditors offered their surpluses from the resources replenished last week.
"More loans were sought this morning than lately. Some banks did not sell foreign exchange to the central bank (last Wednesday) and needed more money," one dealer told Reuters.
Call money borrowings at a steady 7.0 percent accounted for most of the morning trade.
Banks granted each other 10-day funds at 9.0 percent and 30-day funds at 11 percent. One insurer accepted a lower nine-percent rate for a 30-day loan to a bank.
The 50- and 60-day interbank deals were struck at 12 and 13 percent, respectively.
Banks had repaid all but 0.75 million in Lombard loans to the central bank last week and did not increase their borrowing this morning, a bank official said.
They ended last Saturday with 712.6 million kuna on their balances, with minimal shortfalls after the central bank paid them 454 million kuna for the purchase of hard currency.
Saturday's overnight money market trade was less than three million kuna as only one bank borrowed money to square position and another for the statutory reserve.
The market is closed on Tuesday due to public holiday. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb newsroom +385 1 455 7075
